title: Derivation of the Impulse-Momentum Theorem
governing_principles: Newton's Second Law in momentum form \vec{F} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}
Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for definite vector integrals
assumptions: Continuous or piecewise continuous force over finite time interval [t_1, t_2]

derivation_steps.description: Express Newton's Second Law as the time rate of change of linear momentum.
Multiply by infinitesimal time increment dt to formulate differential momentum change.
Integrate both sides between initial state 1 and final state 2.
Evaluate the left side to obtain the net momentum change, which equals impulse J.

limiting_cases: Constant force F: J = F (t2 - t1) = F Delta t.
Zero force: J = 0 implies Delta p = 0 (conservation of momentum).
dimensional_check: Both impulse and momentum change have dimensions [M][L][T]^-1 (N s or kg m/s).
source_provenance: HCV1 Ch 9 p. 159; HRW Ch 9 p. 238; UP Ch 8 p. 268
